newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European stocks slip with Dow, dollar steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European stocks slip with Dow, dollar steady.

text.p: European bourses opened down on Thursday in line with a sharply lower overnight close of the Dow Jones industrial average as profit-takers held the market back from piercing a key target level.
German and Italian shares pulled back from their record highs on Wednesday.

The dollar held mostly steady as traders digested a decision of the German central bank to leave interest rates unchanged and awaited the Bank of England's (BOE) policy meeting for decisions on interest rates. The BOE was widely expected to raise rates.
The dollar hit its highest level against the mark since February 1994, but traders shrugged off the move, and trading volume was low.

In Britain, most analysts predicted the BOE to announce a rate rise at the end of its two-day policy meeting at 1100 GMT. Traders said the markets have priced in a 25-basis point rise in the 6.5-percent base rate but would not be surprised if rates jumped a half point to keep the quick-growing economy from overheating.
"The market is looking for aggressive (BOE) tightening," said a British bank dealer. "Anything less than half a point will see sterling lower."
But if British rates gain more than a quarter point and gives sterling a lift, British export shares would tumble, dealers said.
Export shares have dropped sharply as sterling surged to a 73-month high of 2.9760 marks on Wednesday.
Further pressure on London's FTSE-100 index and other European bourses came from the Dow's 119.88 point-slide overnight.
The Dow's 1.5-percent decline came after two separate but failed attempts earlier in the session to break the key psychological 8,000 barrier.
But losses in France's CAC-40 index and Germany's DAX index were tempered by the dollar's recent strength against their respective currencies.
In Paris, SEB SA was the biggest loser, shedding 4.62 percent to 1,073 French francs by 0925 GMT despite a rise in first-half sales, which traders said was positive.
Eramet was among the winners, jumping 7.59 percent to 312.0, after the company voted to keep chairman Yves Rambaud and the government ordered a new study on New Caledonia mining situation.
Eurotunnel SA holders awaited news from a meeting on debt conversion later in the day. The share was suspended from trading pending the news.
German shares opened bourse trade weaker, with Allianz AG Holding tumbling 16.5 marks to 401.0 by 0930 GMT after it said it expected 1997 group premium income to rise 11 percent.
In metals markets, gold opened little changed amid calm trading. Dealers expected gold prices to drift higher, recovering some of its steep losses to 12-year lows.
"I think we have seen the lows, and the next move is toward $325" this week, a dealer at a major Swiss bank said.
But traders said sentiment remained bearish and that heavy selling could reemerge next week.
CURRENCIES AT 0935 GMT
The dollar was at 112.95 yen and 1.7605 marks compared with 112.97 and 1.7612 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0935 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 15.5 points at 4,746.9.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 66.89 points at 3,988.97.
PARIS - The CAC-40 dropped 15.44 points to 2,935.12.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened in Zurich at $319.60 per ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $319.75. Silver opened there at $4.35, a cent higher than Wednesday's close at $4.34.
